speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation, I am Dr. Agent. Since you are a newborn, I will rely on your parents to describe the symptoms you are experiencing. To begin, how long has your baby been alive, and have there been any specific concerns noted at birth or in the hours since?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that background. Given the lack of prenatal care and immunization, I need to know if your newborn has developed a yellow tint to her skin or eyes (jaundice) or if she has shown poor feeding and lethargy since birth. REQUEST TEST: Bilirubin_level; REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_differential.

speaker: Doctor
text: The lab results show normal bilirubin and blood counts, so let's shift focus to the physical exam. Can you describe exactly what you notice when you hold her, such as any muscle tone issues, breathing irregularities, or abnormalities in her head, eyes, or limbs?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: DiGeorge Syndrome (22q11.2 deletion syndrome).

The combination of a continuous heart murmur (suggesting a Patent Ductus Arteriosus), bluish macules (likely blueberry muffin rash from extramedullary hematopoiesis), cloudy lenses (congenital cataracts), and hearing failure is highly characteristic of this condition, especially given the history of no prenatal care. I will request an echocardiogram and a FISH test for 22q11.2 deletion to confirm this.
